name: Google BigQuery

driver.license: Google Cloud terms (download on this machine; never redistributed)

auth_hint: a service-account sign-in is a token dated by the database's clock, so a clock that is off reads as a refused key - if exakit status shows it behind, restart the database; otherwise the key may be deleted or disabled in Google Cloud
access: BigQuery Job User on the project and BigQuery Data Viewer on the dataset
tips: Names keep BigQuery's spelling (orders, customer_id): quote them, e.g. SELECT "customer_id" FROM <schema>."orders".
INT64 arrives as DECIMAL(19,0) and FLOAT64 as DOUBLE; an ARRAY or STRUCT column arrives as BigQuery's raw JSON text ({"v": ...}).
notes: Rows come back as VALUES from the adapter itself - meant for small results (upstream warns at a few thousand rows). BIGQUERY_ENABLE_IMPORT stays off.

The credential is the service-account key file (JSON) Google Cloud creates, through --password-file. The driver reads it only from a file, so the kit writes it to BucketFS as this source's own file, owner-only on this computer, and the CONNECTION names its path - not the key. Measured: a key in the CONNECTION's password is refused (OAuthPvtKeyPath required).

Any database user who may create scripts can read files in BucketFS. connect and check name such users (other than administrators); today that is nobody on a fresh kit. disconnect and remove delete the key file; reauth replaces it, keeping the previous one when the new one is refused.

Give the service account only BigQuery Job User on the project and BigQuery Data Viewer (READER) on the dataset. The sign-in is a token dated by the database's clock: after the computer slept, restart the database if the key is refused.
